meta.title: HQ System Atlas
meta.claim: HQ is a shared context and capability layer: Core makes work local and legible, Cloud moves state, and Pro makes it shared, secure, and durable.

zones.label: HQ Experience Surfaces
zones.description: Native AI clients, operator tools, web products, installers, meetings, and control surfaces over one scoped system.

zones.label: HQ Core
zones.description: The filesystem context, capability, policy, and execution layer installed with every HQ.

zones.label: HQ Cloud
zones.description: The entity-aware bridge between local HQ state and shared services.

zones.label: HQ Pro
zones.description: Identity, durable shared truth, governance, hosted execution, and commercial control.

capabilities.label: AI clients
capabilities.summary: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cowork, ChatGPT, and Claude.ai consume the same HQ context through native adapters and MCP.
capabilities.detail: HQ is intentionally model-agnostic. Claude and Codex receive native skill, policy, and hook bridges; desktop and hosted chat clients enter through the same guarded MCP facade.

capabilities.label: HQ CLI
capabilities.summary: The local command bus for identity, sync, files, secrets, people, agents, meetings, integrations, billing, and Outposts.
capabilities.detail: The hq command is the stable local boundary between humans, automation, the sync engine, and Pro APIs. It validates scope and translates operator intent into narrow platform operations.

capabilities.label: HQ Desktop
capabilities.summary: Signed desktop clients combine onboarding, long-lived sync, company activity, meetings, agents, deployments, secrets, and updates.
capabilities.detail: The consolidated desktop repo ships a native SwiftUI/AppKit macOS client and a retained Tauri/Svelte Windows client on one service contract and release policy.

capabilities.label: HQ Console
capabilities.summary: The tenant-aware web workspace for companies, people, agents, knowledge, files, secrets, integrations, billing, deployments, and operations.
capabilities.detail: Console projects Pro's durable authority into a navigable browser experience. It is an operator surface, not a second source of truth, and every route resolves identity and company scope first.

capabilities.label: Auth + onboarding
capabilities.summary: Sign-in, account recovery, company creation, invitations, membership acceptance, and first-run education establish a scoped HQ identity.
capabilities.detail: HQ Auth owns the independent authentication surface while HQ Onboarding guides people through company and product setup. Both hand a verified identity into Pro's membership model.

capabilities.label: Install + bootstrap
capabilities.summary: The create-hq bootstrapper and native Installer turn a blank machine into an authenticated, configured, updateable HQ.
capabilities.detail: create-hq handles terminal-first setup and repository bootstrap; HQ Installer provides a guided native distribution path. Both converge on the same Core layout, identity, and update contract.

capabilities.label: HQ Meet
capabilities.summary: A decentralized virtual office for encrypted video, audio, screen sharing, rooms, moderation, and direct file transfer.
capabilities.detail: HQ Meet has no accounts or cloud authority and is intentionally separate from Pro's recorded-meeting intelligence. A lightweight relay carries signaling; media and files move peer-to-peer over libp2p and WebRTC.

capabilities.label: HQ Meta
capabilities.summary: A dependency-light client and CLI for tenant-safe Meta ad accounts, campaigns, ad sets, ads, and bounded insights.
capabilities.detail: HQ Meta reads a company-specific token only through HQ vault injection, constrains every account read through a connected-account ledger, and emits structured redacted output for agents and operators.

capabilities.label: HQ Finance
capabilities.summary: A dedicated finance surface for subscriptions, usage, commercial records, and operator reconciliation.
capabilities.detail: Finance interprets Pro billing and metering records for authorized operators while Stripe and Pro remain the commercial systems of record.

capabilities.label: HQ Ops
capabilities.summary: An internal package-registry admin for versions, entitlements, licenses, downloads, tenant assignments, and usage.
capabilities.detail: HQ Ops is the legacy Clerk and Mongo administration surface. Modern marketplace identity, listings, entitlements, and commercial authority primarily live in Pro, Console, and CLI.

capabilities.label: HQ operating layer
capabilities.summary: Resolves context, routes capabilities, enforces policy, coordinates work, and records state across AI tools.
capabilities.detail: The Core kernel is a shipped filesystem scaffold rather than a daemon. It binds the active company, project, repo, policies, packs, workers, skills, hooks, and knowledge to each work session.

capabilities.label: Companies + overlays
capabilities.summary: Company folders isolate tenant knowledge, policies, settings, workers, projects, and registries; personal customizations live separately.
capabilities.detail: The manifest resolves ownership and service bindings. Company context is fail-closed, and personal overlays never weaken tenant boundaries.

capabilities.label: Sessions + continuity
capabilities.summary: Checkpoints, handoffs, journals, thread locks, and recovery preserve work across context windows, people, and machines.
capabilities.detail: Canonical thread records live under workspace; project journals capture decisions and open loops; company mirrors make the audit trail tenant-readable without changing authority.

capabilities.label: Plans + projects
capabilities.summary: Ideas become reviewed PRDs, dependency-aware stories, and Work Mesh-visible execution with explicit done criteria.
capabilities.detail: Planning and execution are separate phases. Stories carry priority, evidence, acceptance criteria, state, and worker routing; Work Mesh provides live coordination without replacing the PRD.

capabilities.label: Workers + skills
capabilities.summary: Specialized workers bundle instructions, skills, context, verification, and tool access behind a stable execution contract.
capabilities.detail: Workers can be public, personal, or company-specific. Packs add coherent capability bundles; plugins can contribute skills, apps, MCP servers, hooks, knowledge, and policies.

capabilities.label: Policies + quality gates
capabilities.summary: Policies, hooks, tests, review, file locks, and approval gates turn institutional rules into execution-time constraints.
capabilities.detail: HQ applies the narrowest relevant company, repo, and global rules. Quality gates do not replace judgment; they make unsafe or incomplete paths observable and blockable.

capabilities.label: Knowledge + search
capabilities.summary: Public, personal, and company knowledge combines curated docs, qmd search, ontology, meetings, signals, and source provenance.
capabilities.detail: Knowledge remains files first. INDEX files provide deterministic navigation, qmd adds semantic/full-text retrieval, and ontology and signal systems add structured interpretation without replacing source material.

capabilities.label: Packs + MCP
capabilities.summary: Versioned packages extend HQ with capabilities while one guarded MCP facade exposes the same context to local and hosted clients.
capabilities.detail: Pack manifests declare contributions and host requirements. MCP registration targets both Claude and Codex, while the server facade centralizes company scope, path guards, write guards, and verb whitelists.

capabilities.label: Repos + code
capabilities.summary: Public and private repositories stay code-only while HQ supplies tenant context, project state, workers, and policy around them.
capabilities.detail: The orchestration root and product repos remain separate trust and release domains. Repo-specific policies and explicit git anchors prevent cross-repo drift.

capabilities.label: Learning loop
capabilities.summary: Corrections, retrospectives, releases, and reusable findings flow back into scoped policy, knowledge, skills, and worker instructions.
capabilities.detail: Learnings are routed to the narrowest durable home rather than accumulated in a universal prompt. Documentation sync keeps shipped behavior and public explanation aligned.

capabilities.label: Entity-aware bridge
capabilities.summary: Plans and executes scoped movement between a local HQ tree and the authoritative services for the active person and companies.
capabilities.detail: Modern HQ Cloud is the sync/client library used by HQ CLI and Desktop. It is not the older NanoClaw hosted-agent runtime still visible on an obsolete checkout branch.

capabilities.label: Sync planner
capabilities.summary: Discovery, hashing, journals, pull records, tombstones, conflict mirrors, and currency gates make bidirectional sync recoverable.
capabilities.detail: Push, pull, and both modes reconcile per-company and personal scopes. Deletion requires currency evidence; conflicts surface for human resolution instead of silent overwrite.

capabilities.label: Realtime wakeups
capabilities.summary: SQS, SNS, AWS IoT, and push notifications wake clients quickly while polling and durable stores remain the correctness backstop.
capabilities.detail: Realtime channels carry signals, not canonical history. Clients always reconcile against durable state after a wakeup, reconnect, or missed event.

capabilities.label: Shared files
capabilities.summary: Scoped file listing, transfer, share sessions, recovery, and presigned access expose company vault content without flattening ACLs.
capabilities.detail: Clients receive narrowly scoped credentials or presigned operations. The service keeps file authority in Pro and object authority in per-entity storage.

capabilities.label: Secrets execution
capabilities.summary: Metadata, grants, one-time submission, and process injection keep values out of files, stdout, and chat transcripts.
capabilities.detail: Secrets are company-scoped capabilities. Agents receive only the values and destinations they are authorized to use, with reads and executions audited.

capabilities.label: HQ MCP
capabilities.summary: One company-scoped facade exposes identity, knowledge, projects, files, policies, and safe operations over local stdio and cloud HTTP.
capabilities.detail: The transport changes; the guards do not. Both local and cloud entrypoints share the same registry, path guard, scope guard, and verb whitelist.

capabilities.label: HQ Map
capabilities.summary: A generated company knowledge graph connects entities, sources, meetings, signals, projects, and relationships for Console exploration.
capabilities.detail: HQ Map is a product feature, distinct from this public System Atlas. Its generated graph is derived from authorized company knowledge and rendered inside tenant scope.

capabilities.label: HQ Deploy
capabilities.summary: Static artifacts, server apps, and sleeping SSR workloads ship with custom domains, access policies, bindings, analytics, and usage controls.
capabilities.detail: Deploy handles packaging, queues, DNS, runtime selection, access mode, and wake/sleep behavior. Sensitive artifacts stay behind explicit policy rather than URL obscurity.

capabilities.label: Messages + activity
capabilities.summary: Direct messages, notifications, company activity, agent sessions, meetings, and deployment events converge into shared surfaces.
capabilities.detail: Desktop, Console, and connected channels render durable server state and use push signals for freshness. Agent and Slack session diagnostics intentionally exclude secret material.

capabilities.label: Platform authority
capabilities.summary: The authoritative control plane for tenant identity, shared state, permissions, hosted execution, integrations, and commercial policy.
capabilities.detail: Pro is broader than its original Vault framing. DynamoDB and per-entity object stores hold durable truth; services issue scoped capabilities and project that truth into Console, Desktop, CLI, MCP, and agent runtimes.

capabilities.label: Identity + SSO
capabilities.summary: Cognito-backed person identity, federated sign-in, provider linking, session exchange, and app authentication establish the caller.
capabilities.detail: HQ Auth centralizes web SSO while CLI, Desktop, Console, MCP, and machine sessions exchange only the tokens needed for their specific boundary.

capabilities.label: Entities + membership
capabilities.summary: Person and company entities, memberships, roles, invites, groups, and activation state define tenant participation.
capabilities.detail: Company UIDs, not slugs or email alone, are the durable boundary. Membership and group projections feed every access, collaboration, billing, and provisioning decision.

capabilities.label: Vault + ACL
capabilities.summary: Per-entity S3/KMS vaults, path ACLs, groups, capability-vended access, audit, and secret classification protect shared state.
capabilities.detail: Deny-all storage is opened through narrow, short-lived capabilities. Object stores hold bytes; DynamoDB holds entity, ACL, grant, audit, and provisioning truth.

capabilities.label: Work Mesh
capabilities.summary: Durable threads, claims, leases, progress, blockers, questions, handoffs, participants, and facets coordinate human and agent work.
capabilities.detail: Work Mesh is live coordination around a project; it does not replace the PRD or source repo. Local helpers and remote agents write through guarded APIs, with MQTT/IoT used only for fan-out.

capabilities.label: Agents + Outposts
capabilities.summary: Fleet agents, boxes, jobs, channel sessions, desired state, storage, health, incidents, and kill switches run work beyond a laptop.
capabilities.detail: Hosted execution preserves the same company-scoped HQ root and capability model. Outposts and boxes receive narrow machine identity, mounted context, and explicit lifecycle controls.

capabilities.label: Knowledge pipeline
capabilities.summary: Meetings, sources, signals, ontology, vector search, graph construction, and knowledge workers turn evidence into scoped context.
capabilities.detail: Recorded meeting intelligence and HQ Meet are separate systems. Pro ingests authorized sources and projections, then makes them searchable and inspectable through scoped APIs and surfaces.

capabilities.label: Integrations + MCP
capabilities.summary: OAuth connections, tool grants, Integration MCP, confirmation queues, sidecars, and audited writes connect external systems.
capabilities.detail: A connection is tenant-scoped and a tool grant is capability-scoped. Mutating actions can require confirmation and idempotency rather than trusting the chat surface.

capabilities.label: Marketplace
capabilities.summary: Creators, listings, skills, workers, packs, security review, versioning, and entitlements distribute reusable capability.
capabilities.detail: Marketplace packages are installed into the local Core extension model while Pro owns identity, listing, entitlement, and commercial records.

capabilities.label: Billing + limits
capabilities.summary: Plans, Stripe subscriptions, seat and agent pricing, usage metering, sponsorships, limits, and overrides govern paid capacity.
capabilities.detail: Commercial state is tenant-aware and feeds provisioning and access decisions. Metering and enforcement remain separate so operators can audit what was measured and why it was blocked.

capabilities.label: Health + incidents
capabilities.summary: Telemetry, feedback, monitors, alarms, agent incidents, deployment state, and status projections keep the platform observable.
capabilities.detail: Signals become durable incident or feedback records with owner, lifecycle, evidence, and closure. Live checks verify user-facing paths rather than trusting enqueue or deploy signals.

capabilities.label: Delivery orchestration
capabilities.summary: Serialized deployment queues, tenant stacks, CodeBuild, app access policy, API keys, and release evidence move artifacts into production.
capabilities.detail: Pro coordinates durable deployment intent and platform credentials while HQ Deploy owns application hosting and Core owns review, release, documentation, and learning discipline.

tour.title: One operating system, three planes
tour.claim: Core, Cloud, and Pro are separate authorities that compose into one user experience.
tour.body: Core owns local context and execution. Cloud moves and projects scoped state. Pro owns identity, durable shared truth, governance, and hosted runtime.

tour.title: Meet people where they already work
tour.claim: People enter HQ through native AI clients, CLI, desktop, web, installers, and focused products with explicit trust boundaries.
tour.body: Most surfaces converge on company scope, guarded capabilities, and Pro authority. HQ Meet remains a deliberately independent peer-to-peer product with no accounts or cloud authority.

tour.title: Core turns a filesystem into a team operating layer
tour.claim: Context is useful because it is routed, scoped, executable, and resumable—not because it is merely stored.
tour.body: Company overlays, sessions, PRDs, workers, policies, knowledge, packs, repos, and learnings form the local work system every supported AI client inherits.

tour.title: Work survives the context window
tour.claim: Checkpoint, handoff, journals, locks, and Work Mesh make continuity an explicit protocol.
tour.body: Local thread state preserves reasoning and open loops; Pro coordinates live owners, progress, blockers, questions, and handoffs across people and agents.

tour.title: Intent moves through back-pressure
tour.claim: HQ separates planning, execution, verification, shipping, and learning so autonomy stays auditable.
tour.body: PRDs shape the work; workers and skills execute; policy, tests, review, and approvals gate it; repos and deploy planes ship it; evidence feeds the learning loop.

tour.title: Cloud moves state without becoming the source of truth
tour.claim: Bidirectional sync is recoverable because transfer records, tombstones, conflict mirrors, and durable authority are separate.
tour.body: HQ Cloud plans and performs transfers. Realtime events only wake clients. Pro remains authoritative for entities, ACLs, files, messages, and shared state.

tour.title: Every capability crosses a trust boundary
tour.claim: Identity answers who, tenancy answers where, and grants answer what—before data or tools are exposed.
tour.body: Cognito sessions, memberships, company UIDs, path ACLs, groups, scoped credentials, secret injection, policy hooks, and audit logs layer together.

tour.title: Agents are teammates with runtime state
tour.claim: Hosted agents inherit the same company context and capability model, then add boxes, schedules, health, sessions, and incident controls.
tour.body: Outposts and fleet agents run beyond a laptop while Work Mesh keeps ownership and progress visible and Realtime keeps surfaces fresh.

tour.title: Evidence becomes shared intelligence
tour.claim: Files stay canonical while search, meetings, sources, signals, ontology, vectors, and graphs make them usable.
tour.body: Core curates and retrieves local knowledge. Pro ingests authorized shared evidence and produces scoped projections such as HQ Map for Console and agents.

tour.title: Pro turns capability into a managed platform
tour.claim: Integrations, marketplace, billing, health, and delivery make the operating layer governable at company scale.
tour.body: Connected apps receive explicit grants, reusable capability is distributed through the marketplace, commercial rules govern capacity, and platform evidence closes the loop.
